text:
Eli: heads-up — multiple customers reporting 503s starting ~10m ago. dashboards (link: https://grafana.redwood/alerts) show upstream_error_rate spike on hosted-us-west-2
Maria: seeing the same. error pattern looks like upstream worker crashes (SIGSEGV) in inference pool for model-rex-13b-q4
Kevin: confirmed via logs from upstream-worker-az3-ptl-9:
```
Nov 15 14:52:03 upstream-worker[pid=8421]: segfault at 0 ip 0x7f3a2f1a2f sp 0x7ffd6b1c
Nov 15 14:52:03 trace: cuCtxSynchronize() failed: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION
Nov 15 14:52:03 containerd: killing container upstream-worker-az3-ptl-9 (exit_code=139)
```
Eli: customer impact - ticket #ACME-4123 opened by Acme Corp, low-volume inference calls intermittently returning 503, started about 14:52 PST
SupportBot: pinging customers with status page update template.
Maria: repro attempt on staging: ran repeated calls against rex-13b-q4 with batch_size=8 and short prompt, got worker crash after ~600 requests.
Alex: what's the GPU driver version on affected nodes?
Kevin: rolling list: nvidia-driver 525.85.05 on az3 nodes, mixed with some 530.x on others. the failures cluster on 525 nodes.
InfraOncall: priority: isolate and cordon the affected hosts, draining upstream pool for az3. I'm starting a drain on pool-hosts tag=az3-ptl now
Eli: can we put automatic fallback to next compatible model (rex-13b-fp16) for hosted requests? We have a fallback policy but it didn't trigger because variants flagged as incompatible for seq_len > 1024
Maria: temporarily enabling fallback for this customer to rex-13b-fp16 for Acme Corp only (routing rule created). will monitor for errors reducing.
Kevin: collecting core dump from container; attaching ps + nvidia-smi output:
```
PID   GPU_MEM_USED  CPU%  COMMAND
8421  13700MiB      74.3  /usr/bin/infer-runner --model rex-13b-q4
nvidia-smi: GPU 0 has 24GiB total, 22.1GiB used, temp 79C
```
Maria: interesting: memory usage not at absolute max but KV cache spike correlates with short prompts pattern, maybe a fragmentation issue after many seq_len=2048 warmups
Alex: reproduce script I'm running:
```
for i in {1..2000}; do curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"model":"rex-13b-q4","input":"${i}_hello","max_tokens":32,"batch":8}' https://api.redwood/complete || echo "fail $i"; done
```
Kevin: stacktrace from core (partial):
```
#0 0x7f3a2f1a2f in attn_backward() + 0x2f
#1 0x7f3a2f2900 in kv_cache_update + 0x120
#2 0x55a3d0 in infer_loop
```
Eli: initial hypothesis: attention kernel illegal instruction or memory access pattern causing SIGSEGV on driver 525.85.05 with q4 runtime kernel. 530 drivers seem unaffected.
InfraOncall: rolling a canary: updating az3 nodes to driver 530.41.03 one at a time, will report back.
DeployBot: triggered hotfix deploy: revert quantization patch from last week to revert to older attn kernel. canary rollout to 10% of upstream pool at 15:20 PST
Maria: after enabling fallback for Acme and canary revert, error rate dropped ~80% for that customer. other customers on az3 still seeing ~30% of spike.
Kevin: we captured an illegal-instruction signal in the container logs that points to a new avx512 variant compiled into attn kernel; older GPU/driver combos choke on it.
Alex: do we have build artifacts with ISA checks? Probably need runtime guard for instruction set.
Eli: mitigation plan: 1) continue driver rollouts on affected hosts 2) rollback quant patch fully in next 30m if driver's rollout not reducing errors 3) enable conservative kernel selection (disable AVX512 path) for q4 runtime 4) follow-up postmortem and alert rule tuned
SupportBot: updated incident page with mitigation steps and ETA 30m. customers notified.
InfraOncall: node drain in progress, 6/24 hosts cordoned in az3 pool. autoscaler holding capacity.
Maria: recording minimal repro steps for postmortem: single client script with batch=8, burst QPS=80, seq_len=512-2048, observed crash after ~500-700 calls. attaching logs to ticket.
Kevin: created patch to runtime to skip AVX512 path when driver < 530. pushed to staging, running regression harness now.
Alex: can we tweak the retry policy at gateway to avoid immediate 503 surfacing to customers? maybe add 2s exponential backoff + 2 retries for remote failures
Eli: agreed, please coordinate with API team. Sarah from API is offline but I'll loop her in after triage.
SupportBot: Customer ACME-4123 notified of temporary routing change and ongoing remediation.
InfraOncall: driver rollout progress: 10/24 updated, crashes reduced on updated nodes. we will continue and monitor for any perf regressions.
Maria: logging follow-ups: will paste minimal kernel backtrace and sample pcap of request pattern in the postmortem doc.
Kevin: ETA to full rollback of quant patch if needed: 45m (manual validation + canary)
Eli: filing a Sev-2 incident doc, will capture timeline, RCA drivers vs runtime codegen, and action items (driver pin recommendations, kernel guards, rollback playbook).
Alex: noted for next release: add runtime telemetry for instruction set path taken per request so we can correlate going forward
Eli: thanks everyone. I'll keep this thread updated and escalate to eng-management if error rate doesn't hit baseline in 1h :rotating_light:
SupportBot: incident severity set to P1 and flagged in pager duty.
Maria: adding link to postmortem draft: https://docs.redwood/incidents/2067890123-draft
Kevin: will follow-up with PR link once runtime guard is merged.
Eli: closing loop for now; last check 15:40 PST error rate at ~5% over baseline. will re-open if regression. :thumbsup:
